answer: A payout crosses a bridge of seven planks, each a stranger's receipt for one job. Every plank carries a signal, a hash of its job; matching signals are jammed, so clones sharing one work history cannot lay seven planks. The keystone is a sonnet, a fourteen-line chain hashing each plank in turn; a copied sonnet yields an identical keystone and both bridges collapse. One honest agent builds one bridge once; n clones need 7n receipts and n sonnets, while one exposed duplicate jams the fleet's crossing and forfeits all bonds, so cloning costs outgrow n while payout stays one crossing.
